transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Aisha (Veridian EM), Tom (Veridian Platform), Rachel (Veridian DS)

Summary: quick SDK walkthrough (Python + TypeScript), auth and env setup for hosted API, quickstart snippets, discussion about Dedicated vs hosted for latency/cost, and pilot next steps. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the SDK quickstart and auth flows, and Diego will do a short live demo. Aisha, Tom, Rachel, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Aisha: thanks lena, excited to see the flow - we mainly want to know how fast we can get a POC up and running and what infra we need.
[00:22] Diego: awesome, quick intro - i'm diego, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll jump into the code examples, show python and ts snippets and the console bits. Lena will cover commercial and next steps.
[00:35] Tom: hi, quick note - we run on k8s EKS, some services in GCP, but prefer a VPC peering or private endpoint for data-sensitive calls. also curious about service account auth versus user tokens.
[00:47] Diego: yeah totally, we'll show both. Redwood supports API key auth for hosted, and for private/dedicated we support mTLS and service accounts with short lived tokens, plus KMS/HSM integration for keys.
[01:05] Rachel: for the DS team, main question is latency for short chat-ish prompts and embeddings for similarity search. cost matters too.
[01:14] Diego: makes sense. We'll highlight batching, prefix caching and quantization recommendations in Optimize that reduce token cost.

-- Quickstart and Auth --
[02:02] Diego: starting with python quickstart, here's the minimal snippet: import redwood; client = redwood.Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.chat.create(model='rwd-2b', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'summarize sales chat'}]) - response is streaming by default.
[02:25] Laptop typing noise / brief pause
[02:35] Diego: note that in some transcriptions that function name comes out weird, but it's client.chat.create in the SDK. For ts: import {Redwood} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-2b', messages: [...] });
[03:05] Tom: is there an official npm and pip package? versions?
[03:10] Diego: yep pip package named redwood-inference and npm @redwood/inference. We maintain release notes in the repo and semver. The quickstart repo link i'll share after the call.
[03:24] Aisha: how do we set env for multiple environments? dev/test/prod?
[03:30] Diego: best practice - use per-environment API keys, store them in secret manager (GCP Secret Manager or AWS Secrets Manager). For private deployments you can issue service account creds and rotate them. You can also use RBAC in Console to restrict keys to routes.
[03:50] Rachel: any gotchas for streaming in node?
[03:54] Diego: main thing is backpressure on your consumer, we provide event-based streams and also chunked http streaming. In ts quickstart we show using the sdk.stream method and a small example of reconnect logic.

-- Console demo (observability + Optimize) --
[05:10] Diego: switching to the console, here's the per-route latency heatmap, you can filter by model and route. The optimize tab will suggest batching window and quantization level for your workload. For ecomm-ish prompts it suggested a 64-token prefix cache and dynamic batching window 50-200ms.
[05:38] Slight mouse clicks
[05:45] Aisha: can you export those recommendations? we want to add them to infra runbook.
[05:49] Diego: yes PDF/CSV export available and we'll include the snapshot in the quickstart link.

-- Dedicated vs Hosted discussion --
[06:20] Tom: we need predictable p95 latency, spikes during flash sales are a concern. Looking at costs, dedicated makes sense if sustained throughput is high - can you give thresholds?
[06:36] Lena: generally customers seeing Dedicated ROI when they exceed ~40-60M tokens/month but it depends on model size and request patterns. Diego, feel free to add nuance.
[06:46] Diego: yeah for chat with 2k token windows you hit different economics. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and you can pin models. Hosted has autoscale and is faster to start. For bursty patterns we recommend dedicated with burst capacity configured or hybrid route policies to overflow to hosted.
[07:08] Rachel: hybrid route policy meaning some requests go to hosted for overflow?
[07:12] Diego: exactly, policy-based routing by latency SLO or cost threshold, and auto-fallback when capacity is constrained.

-- Security / Compliance --
[07:40] Tom: for private data we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO, full KMS integration. any limitations?
[07:49] Lena: we have SOC2, SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning, audit logs in console, and KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments. For hosted we do not keep raw customer prompt content beyond configured retention windows, and you can opt out of data retention for enterprise contracts.
[08:10] Aisha: does the SDK handle token rotation or is that on us?
[08:14] Diego: SDK reads keys from env - rotation handled by your secret manager; for private/dedicated we can wire service account tokens and short lived creds, we also provide examples for automatic refresh in the quickstart.

-- Live code walkthrough (python) --
[09:00] Diego: i'll paste a little integrated example for embeddings and caching. code: client = redwood.Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), cache_config={'prefix_cache': True}); emb = client.embeddings.create(model='rwd-embed-1', input='product description'); this returns a vector you can store in your vector DB.
[09:25] Rachel: do you integrate with vector DBs or provide managed similarity?
[09:29] Diego: we integrate with popular vector stores (pinecone, milvus, etc) via SDK adapters and also provide similarity reranking in the console as a managed feature.
[09:45] Aisha: for the pilot we plan two flows: 1) embeddings for search, 2) short chat responses for product Q&A. latency SLO is p95 < 250ms for chat.
[09:58] Diego: we'll validate that in the bench. note that p95 includes network egress; with Dedicated in-region you'll see better tail latency.

-- Quickstarts & repo links --
[11:20] Diego: quick note on the repo layout: examples/python/quickstart.py, examples/ts/quickstart.ts, infra/helm chart for private, docs/security.md. i'll share link - it's public but we can make a private sandbox repo for the pilot.
[11:40] Tom: can you show how we mint a scoped key limited to embeddings only?
[11:45] Diego: yes in console -> API keys -> create scoped key -> select scopes -> embeddings only -> set expiration. SDK reads it same way. Console also shows usage and route limits.
[12:05] Aisha: what about rate limits and retries? we have bursty patterns during campaigns.
[12:12] Diego: we expose rate-limiting config per-key and have client-side exponential backoff recommended in the quickstart. For Dedicated you can increase capacity and set autoscale policies.

-- Integration pitfalls & gotchas --
[13:00] Diego: common gotchas: 1) forgetting to pin model version leading to drift; 2) not enabling prefix cache for templated prompts; 3) using too large batch sizes causing latency spikes; 4) not instrumenting token usage which can surprise cost.
[13:20] Rachel: about model pinning - can we pin to a minor model release and still get security fixes?
[13:27] Diego: yes you can pin minor semver or allow automatic security patches via a pinned policy - console supports controlled rollout.

-- Pricing & Commercials brief --
[14:10] Lena: for ballpark - hosted per-token pricing for medium models, embeddings priced per vector, Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly fee and lower per-token runtime. we'll send a tailored pricing sheet after we get your traffic profile.
[14:25] Aisha: timeline: we want a POC in 2-3 weeks if possible.
[14:30] Lena: doable, Diego will run a bench and we'll provide the quickstart and sample prompts.

-- Recap & Next steps --
[15:00] Lena: recap: we'll share quickstart repo, security docs, and pricing. Diego will set up the pilot bench with Tom and Rachel; Tom will share traffic profile and sample prompts. We'll aim to start the POC week of Dec 8.
[15:18] Tom: sounds good. I'll get the infra details and sample workload over by Monday.
[15:25] Rachel: i'll prepare sample prompts and evaluation criteria.
[15:30] Aisha: please include a short runbook for rollout and for fallback to hosted.
[15:35] Diego: will do; quick reminder the optimize suggestions and console export will be attached.
[15:45] Lena: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff and share the repo and docs.
[15:52] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription: minor mis-hears on k-v cache (sometimes as K-V), slight overlap at 03:24, and a brief dropout while Diego switched screens at 05:38.

References shared: quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (will share access), security whitepaper: /files/redwood-security.pdf (link to be sent), pilot bench spreadsheet (will be shared via email).

End of transcript.
